answer: Unique Challenge-Response Intake. At registration, the system generates a fresh challenge seeded by a public beacon plus a secret kept at a low-traffic wharf, so no challenge repeats. An agent must answer by submitting a computation whose output the issuer cannot predict in advance, then confirm it through a one-time inlet code delivered to a separate channel. The whisper of prior solutions is useless because each challenge invalidates copied answers. An attacker must obtain fresh compute and a distinct channel per identity, paying full cost each time.
